final_text:
Here’s what the network looks like when we take the top HbA1c-associated exposures (fully adjusted model) and then cluster them by how strongly they co-occur (exposure–exposure correlations among the top 30, edges kept for |r| > 0.25 with Bonferroni control). All correlations that survived were positive (147 edges; none negative), so clusters represent co-exposure patterns.

Main clusters and what they represent

1) Organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) — legacy agricultural/termite pesticides concentrated in animal fats
- Members: oxychlordane (LBXOXY), trans-nonachlor (LBXTNA), heptachlor epoxide (LBXHPE), dieldrin (LBXDIE), p,p’-DDT (LBXPDT), p,p’-DDE (LBXPDE), beta-hexachlorocyclohexane (LBXBHC/LBDBHC).
- Within-cluster links: very strong; examples — oxychlordane–trans-nonachlor r=0.916; DDE–DDT r=0.642; heptachlor epoxide–oxychlordane r=0.706; β-HCH–DDE r≈0.72.
- Cross-links: tightly connected to PCBs and moderately to dioxins/furans, reflecting shared persistence and lipid-phase transport.

2) Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) — industrial POPs from electrical equipment, building materials, and contaminated foods (especially fatty fish/dairy)
- Members: PCB74 (LBX074), PCB118 (LBX118, mono-ortho), PCB138 (LBX138), PCB170 (LBX170), PCB187 (LBX187), and the coplanar dioxin-like PCB “pncb” (LBXPCB).
- Within-cluster links: very strong; examples — PCB170–PCB187 r=0.925; PCB74–PCB118 r=0.909; PCB138–PCB170 r=0.891.
- Cross-links: strong ties to OCPs (e.g., PCB118–trans-nonachlor r≈0.68; PCB74–trans-nonachlor r≈0.69) and to dioxins/furans (e.g., PCB74–OCDD r≈0.63; PCB118–HxCDF r≈0.58).

3) Dioxins and furans — combustion/by-product POPs (incineration, metal/chemical production, historic bleaching)
- Members: OCDD (LBXD07), HxCDD (LBXD02), HxCDF (LBXF04), PeCDF (LBXF03).
- Within-cluster links: moderate–strong; examples — OCDD–HxCDF r=0.622; HxCDD–HxCDF r=0.569; HxCDD–OCDD r=0.553.
- Cross-links: connect both to PCBs (e.g., OCDD–PCB “pncb” r=0.551; HxCDF–PCB170 r=0.557) and to OCPs (e.g., OCDD–oxychlordane r=0.608), forming a larger POP “mega-cluster.”

4) Serum fatty acids (dietary/metabolic lipid markers) — reflect dietary fat patterns and co-transport of lipophilic POPs
- Members: oleic (LBXOL1), palmitic (LBXPM1), margaric C17:0 (LBXMRG), docosatetraenoic n-6 (LBXDTA), eicosenoic 20:1 (LBXEN1), myristic 14:0 (LBXMR1).
- Within-cluster links: very strong; examples — oleic–palmitic r=0.919; margaric–oleic r=0.754; docosatetraenoic–palmitic r=0.655.
- Role: a lipid/metabolic cluster that can correlate indirectly with POPs (shared lipophilicity and dietary fat sources), though the strongest edges are within fatty acids themselves.

5) Fat‑soluble vitamins/antioxidants — diet-derived, especially from oils (vitamin E) and fruits/vegetables (carotenoids)
- Vitamin E subcluster: gamma‑tocopherol (LBXGTC, LB2GTC) with d‑tocopherol (LBXDTC); very strong links (gamma–gamma r=0.846; d‑tocopherol–gamma r=0.718).
- Carotenoid/retinoid subcluster: alpha‑carotene (LB2ALC), trans‑beta‑carotene (LB2BEC), beta‑cryptoxanthin (LB2CRY), lutein/zeaxanthin (LB2LUZ), retinol (LB2VIA); moderate–strong links (alpha–beta carotene r=0.746; beta‑cryptoxanthin–lutein/zeaxanthin r=0.570; several ~0.50 range).
- Interpretation: two tightly knit dietary micronutrient groups; gamma‑tocopherol was one of the HbA1c hits (FDR-significant), but it clusters most strongly with other tocopherols.

Isolated/weakly connected among HbA1c hits
- o‑Toluidine (URXOTD, urinary aromatic amine) did not form edges ≥0.25 in this network, indicating it did not cluster with the POPs/lipid/micronutrient groups at the retained significance threshold.

How the clusters fit together
- POP mega‑cluster: OCPs, PCBs, and dioxins/furans are densely interlinked, consistent with shared persistence, lipophilicity, and co-exposure via animal fat–rich foods and legacy environmental reservoirs.
- Lipid/micronutrient clusters: fatty acids and fat‑soluble vitamins form their own tightly connected groups; they reflect dietary patterns and serum lipid milieu. These can align with higher POP body burdens due to co-transport in lipids, but the strongest edges observed were within each of these clusters.
- All retained correlations were positive, indicating these exposures tend to rise together in the population.

Notes on HbA1c associations (for context)
- Among these, gamma‑tocopherol (LBXGTC) and p,p’-DDT (LBXPDT) were FDR‑significant positive correlates of HbA1c in the fully adjusted model. Many other POPs (OCPs/PCBs/dioxins) showed positive but weaker or FDR‑nonsignificant associations; several carotenoids trended negative. These directionally align with the clusters above (POPs co-occur; carotenoids co-occur), but causality cannot be inferred from cross-sectional data.
